지역 중소기업의 AI 격차: 로봇 산업 실증 연구

요* 약

본 연구는 지역 로봇 산업 클러스터 내 중소기업(SMEs) 간의 AI 격차, 즉 인공지능을 도입할 수 있 는 기업과 그렇지 못한 기업 사이의 체계적 간극을 조사하였다. 이를 위해 디지털 격차 이론을 AI 도 입 영역으로 확장하고, 한국의 AI 돌봄 로봇 분야 7개 시·도 소재 52개 중소기업 설문 데이터를 분석하
여 t-검정, 효과크기 분석, 로지스틱 회귀분석을 실시하였다. 분석 결과, 역량 격차가 AI 도입의 압도적
으로 우세한 예측변수(p = .001)로 나타났으며 자원 격차가 그 뒤를 이었다(p = .025). 반면 기술 태도 는 호의적인 점수(M = 4.07/5.0)에도 불구하고 유의미한 효과를 보이지 않았는데, 이는 긍정적 태도가 구속적인 역량 제약으로 인해 실제 도입으로 이어지지 못하는 “인식-도입  역설(awareness-adoption paradox)”을 드러낸다. 본 논문은 태도-행동 격차를 기술수용모델(TAM)의 경계조건으로 식별하고 로봇 산업 내 AI-물리 융합이 도입 장벽을 어떻게 증폭시키는지 밝힘으로써 독창적 가치를 더하며, 실무적으 로는 단순 인식 제고보다 역량 개발과 재정적 지원의 결합이 AI 격차 해소의 핵심임을 시사한다.

ABSTRACT

This study investigates the AI divide among small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) within regional robot  industry  clusters,  defined  as  the  systematic  gap  between  firms  capable  of  adopting  artificial intelligence and  those  that  are  not. Extending  digital  divide  theory  to  the realm  of AI  adoption,  this research analyzes survey data from 52 SMEs in the AI care robot sector across seven Korean provinces.
Using  t-tests, effect size analysis, and logistic regression, we examined the relative effects of competence, resource, and geographical gaps, as well as technological  attitudes, on AI adoption. The findings reveal that the competence gap  is the overwhelmingly dominant predictor of AI adoption (p =  .001), followed by the resource gap (p =  .025). Despite favorable scores (M =  4.07/5.0), technological  attitudes showed no  significant  effect,  uncovering an  “awareness-adoption paradox” where  positive  attitudes  coexist  with non-adoption  due   to  binding  competence   constraints.  This  paper   contributes  by   identifying  the attitude-behavior gap as a boundary condition for the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and clarifying ow AI-physical convergence in the robot industry amplifies specific adoption  barriers. These results ggest that  bridging  the  AI  divide  requires  a  combination  of  capacity  building  and  financial  support,  as awareness  campaigns  alone  are  insufficient  when  competence  and  resource  gaps  act  as  effective constraints.

sections.title: ABSTRACT
sections.content:
This study investigates the AI divide among small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) within regional robot  industry  clusters,  defined  as  the  systematic  gap  between  firms  capable  of  adopting  artificial intelligence and  those  that  are  not. Extending  digital  divide  theory  to  the realm  of AI  adoption,  this research analyzes survey data from 52 SMEs in the AI care robot sector across seven Korean provinces.
Using  t-tests, effect size analysis, and logistic regression, we examined the relative effects of competence, resource, and geographical gaps, as well as technological  attitudes, on AI adoption. The findings reveal that the competence gap  is the overwhelmingly dominant predictor of AI adoption (p =  .001), followed by the resource gap (p =  .025). Despite favorable scores (M =  4.07/5.0), technological  attitudes showed no  significant  effect,  uncovering an  “awareness-adoption paradox” where  positive  attitudes  coexist  with non-adoption  due   to  binding  competence   constraints.  This  paper   contributes  by   identifying  the attitude-behavior gap as a boundary condition for the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and clarifying ow AI-physical convergence in the robot industry amplifies specific adoption  barriers. These results ggest that  bridging  the  AI  divide  requires  a  combination  of  capacity  building  and  financial  support,  as awareness  campaigns  alone  are  insufficient  when  competence  and  resource  gaps  act  as  effective constraints.
